sections.title: Overview
sections.summary: An ordering app for mini savory snacks, built for a single shop, with a customer page and a shop-owner dashboard.

blocks.text: **DeliveryApp** is a portfolio project: a delivery application for one shop. Customers build an order by quantity and flavors, choose delivery or pickup and follow its progress. The shop owner receives orders in a dashboard, changes their status and configures prices, opening hours, Pix and the visual identity.

blocks.title: Public demo
blocks.text: The data is fictional, the dashboard is open to everyone and **all orders are deleted once a day**. Do not enter real personal data. See [Security](#/seguranca) and [Business rules](#/regras-de-negocio) for what is locked in demo mode.

items.title: Customer order
items.text: Quantity (multiples of 10), optional flavors, delivery or pickup, scheduled time, notes and change for cash.

items.title: Payment
items.text: Cash and card (in person) or Pix with a copyable key and a deadline computed by the server.

items.title: Tracking
items.text: A `/pedido/:codigo` page with the status, the estimate and the payment instructions.

items.title: Shop dashboard
items.text: Order list with filters, a sound alert for new orders, status changes and preparation time.

items.title: Settings
items.text: Flavors, price table, delivery fees, opening hours, Pix, name, logos and colors.

items.title: Price always on the server
items.text: The front end only shows a preview. The official amount is computed by the API when the order is created.

items: **Customers:** place an order without creating an account.
**Shop owner:** signs in to the dashboard with a username and password and runs the shop.
**Portfolio reviewers:** can try the demo and read the code.
A single shop (single-tenant) and one kind of product: mini savory snacks.
No customer login: an order is identified by an 8-character code.
No payment gateway: Pix is manual (the customer copies the key) and the shop owner approves the payment.

Delivery is only offered in Paiçandu/PR: the front end shows a notice (`web/src/components/aviso-entrega.tsx`) and tells customers from other cities to pick up. **The API does not validate the city of the address.**

sections.title: Quick start
sections.summary: From clone to a running app in up to three terminals.

items: Node.js 24 and npm.
A PostgreSQL database. The project uses [Neon](https://neon.tech) (the free plan is enough).
To run the API tests: a **second database**, separate from the main one.

blocks.title: Terminal 1
blocks.code:
cd api
npm install
cp .env.example .env      # on PowerShell: Copy-Item .env.example .env
# edit .env: DATABASE_URL, JWT_SECRET, ADMIN_USER and ADMIN_PASSWORD
npm run db:deploy         # creates the tables
npm run db:seed:demo      # fictional data: flavors, prices and the admin
npm run dev               # http://localhost:3333

blocks.text: Check `GET http://localhost:3333/health`. The expected response is `{ "status": "ok" }`.

blocks.title: Terminal 2
blocks.code:
cd web
npm install
npm run dev               # http://localhost:5173

items: Customer: `http://localhost:5173/pedido`
Dashboard: `http://localhost:5173/admin/login` (use the `ADMIN_USER` and `ADMIN_PASSWORD` you set in the API `.env`)

blocks.title: Use port 5173
blocks.text: The API CORS only accepts the `WEB_URL` origin, which defaults to `http://localhost:5173`. If Vite starts on another port, stop whatever is using 5173 or change `WEB_URL`.

On the API, set `MODO_DEMO=false` and run `npm run db:seed` (instead of `db:seed:demo`, which overwrites the configuration). Then, in the dashboard under **Pix and contact**, enter the WhatsApp number, Pix key, account holder and bank. Without the key, the Pix option stays hidden from customers. Also replace `ADMIN_USER` and `ADMIN_PASSWORD` with your own credentials.

blocks.text: `src/server.ts` starts the local server with `listen`. `src/index.ts` exports a serverless handler for Vercel and reuses the Fastify instance between requests. Both use `configurarApp` from `buildApp.ts`, so routes and plugins are identical.

blocks.title: Why Fastify is created in index.ts
blocks.text: The code comment explains two Vercel requirements: the entry file must import `fastify` directly and the `export default` must be a function. That is why `buildApp.ts` has no default export.

sections.summary: From the customer's order to a finished order, and how the shop owner operates.

items: The owner sends a username and password to `POST /auth/login` (limit of 5 per minute).
The API returns a JWT valid for 12 hours. The front end stores the token in `localStorage`.
Every dashboard call sends `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
If the API answers 401, the front end clears the token and goes back to `/admin/login`.

sections.title: Database
sections.summary: PostgreSQL with Prisma. Six tables, one of them a single configuration row.

blocks.caption: Entity-relationship model (main fields).

rows: An order placed by a customer.
Unique 8-character `codigo`. Index on `status, criadoEm`. Stores the subtotal, fee and total already computed.
`saborId` and `quantidade` can be null: a mixed order becomes one item without a flavor. Deleted in cascade with the order.
Never deleted (old orders reference them): removing means deactivating with `ativo = false`.
Parameters the shop owner can adjust.
**Single row with `id = 1`.** Preparation time, fees, Pix, opening hours, pickup address, name, logos and colors.

blocks.text: Migrations live in `api/prisma/migrations/` (there is currently a single, consolidated one). In production use `npm run db:deploy`; to create a new one from schema changes, use `npm run db:migrate` (development only). Apply the migration **before** publishing code that depends on it.

sections.title: Business rules
sections.summary: What the system decides, in product language, with the source in the code.

items: Minimum of 10, maximum of 1000, always in multiples of 10. Source: `services/preco.ts` and `schemas/pedido.ts`.
Up to 100 units: the amount comes from the `FaixaPreco` table.
Above 100: quantity × `valorUnidadeAcimaDe100` (default R$ 0.64).
Calculations use integer cents to avoid rounding errors.
The price is always computed on the server. Source: `services/preco.ts`.
**Mixed** order: no flavors; it becomes a single item without a flavor, displayed as "Misto".
With flavors: either all of them carry a quantity (and the sum must equal the order quantity) or none does (the shop splits it).
A repeated flavor in the same order is rejected.
Only active flavors can be ordered. Deactivated flavors still show in old orders.
Source: `schemas/pedido.ts` and `services/pedidos.ts`.
A Pix order starts as `AGUARDANDO_PAGAMENTO` and goes through `PAGAMENTO_APROVADO`; the others start as `AGUARDANDO`.
Then come `EM_PRODUCAO`, the exit step and `FINALIZADO`.
The exit step is `EM_ROTA_ENTREGA` for delivery and `PRONTO_RETIRADA` for pickup.
The owner can go back one step. Keeping the current status is always accepted. A step that does not exist for that order answers 400.
Source: `statusPermitidos` in `services/pedidos.ts`.
Order for today or "whenever it is ready": pay right away.
Order scheduled for another day: pay up to X hours before the scheduled time. X is 2 hours (default) up to 100 units and 4 hours (default) above that; the owner edits both.
If the computed deadline has already passed, payment is also immediate.
Source: `services/prazoPix.ts`.
Change only applies to cash payments. The banknote value must be **greater** than the order total, otherwise the API answers 400. Source: `services/pedidos.ts`.
All times follow Brasília time (`America/Sao_Paulo`).
**Manually closed:** no orders are accepted, not even scheduled ones.
**Outside opening hours:** only orders scheduled inside the opening hours. Closing time is exclusive (at exactly 18:00 it is already closed).
Hours that cross midnight: the early morning belongs to the day on which the shift started.
With no hours set, the whole day is valid, respecting the service days.
**Delivery off today:** applies only to the day it was turned off. Customers can still schedule delivery for another day.
Source: `services/funcionamento.ts`.

blocks.text: 8 characters drawn from `ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTUVWXYZ23456789`, without I, L, O, 0 and 1 to avoid confusion when read aloud. On a collision the API draws again, up to 5 attempts. Source: `lib/codigo.ts`.

items: CPF and CNPJ are checked by their check digits.
Phone: area code + number; `+55` is accepted and removed when saving, and added back in `chaveParaCopiar`.
Random key: UUID.
`00000000000` is the "key not configured" marker. With it, `configurada` is false and the front end hides the Pix option.
Source: `lib/pix.ts`.

blocks.text: PNG (signature checked) or SVG up to 300 KB. SVGs containing `script`, `foreignObject`, `iframe`, `embed`, `object`, `on*` attributes, `javascript:` or `data:text/html` are rejected. The image is served with long caching and security headers. Source: `lib/logo.ts`.

sections.title: Tests
sections.summary: Vitest in the API and the front end, with a separate database for the API.

items: They use the database from `DATABASE_TESTS_URL` and **refuse to run** if it equals `DATABASE_URL` (`tests/test-env.ts`).
On each run, `tests/global-setup.ts` applies the migrations and the seed to the test database, with the `admin_teste` admin.
Routes are called in memory with `app.inject`, without opening a port.
`MODO_DEMO` is `false` in tests (`vitest.config.ts`). The demo lock is tested by turning the variable on inside the test itself.
Current files: `admin`, `api`, `cors`, `entrega`, `pagamento`, `retirada` and `valores`, in `api/tests/`.

blocks.text: They test the rules in `web/src/lib/` (price, Pix deadline, opening hours, status, theme, logo, formatting and new orders) in `web/src/tests/`. They use neither network nor database.

items: `.github/workflows/api-tests.yml`: installs, type-checks and runs the tests when something in `api/` changes. Needs the repository secret `DATABASE_TESTS_URL`. Runs one execution at a time because of the shared database.
`.github/workflows/web-tests.yml`: installs, builds (types + Vite) and runs the tests when something in `web/` changes.
Pure rule (no database): test the function directly, as in `web/src/tests/preco.test.ts`.
API route: create `api/tests/<topic>.test.ts` and use the utilities in `tests/helpers.ts` with `app.inject`.
Run `npm test` before opening the PR.

sections.title: Project conventions
sections.summary: Conventions observed in the code and in the git history.

items: **Language:** UI, error messages and domain names in Portuguese (`Pedido`, `Sabor`, `criarPedido`).
**TypeScript with ES modules:** relative imports in the API end in `.js`.
**Validation:** every API input goes through a Zod schema; rules that depend on the database live in the services.
**Business errors:** throw `RegraDeNegocioError` (400), `NaoEncontradoError` (404) or `ConflitoError` (409); the central handler in `plugins/erros.ts` turns them into responses.
**Money values:** computed in integer cents and returned as strings with two decimal places.
**Admin routes:** registered inside `routes/admin/index.ts`, which applies the authentication hook to all of them. No admin route is left public by accident.
**Commits:** Conventional Commits-style prefixes, such as `feat(web):`, `fix(api):`, `chore:`, `test(api):` and `docs:`.

blocks.title: To be confirmed
blocks.text: There is no `commitlint`, `husky` or `.editorconfig` in the repository; the commit style looks like an informal convention. Confirm whether it should be enforced. There is also no documented branching policy.

sections.title: Security
sections.summary: Authentication, personal data and the protections already in place.

items: Only the shop owner has a login. The password is stored with bcrypt (cost 12).
Login compares against a fake hash when the user does not exist, so response time does not reveal which users exist.
The JWT is valid for 12 hours and protects **all** routes registered under `routes/admin/`.
The cron route does not use the login: it requires `CRON_SECRET`, compared in constant time.
Rate limit: `POST /pedido` 10 per minute and `POST /auth/login` 5 per minute, per IP (`trustProxy` is on to read the real IP behind Vercel).
CORS is open only to the `WEB_URL` origin, with the methods `GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS`.
Logo upload is limited to a 1 MB body and a 300 KB file, with content validation.
The customer's phone only appears in admin responses; the public order lookup omits it.
The ntfy notification carries no personal data, only code, quantity, type and total.
The front end stores the admin token, theme, sound preference and a branding cache in `localStorage`. No customer data.
In the demo, nothing that is sent should be considered private.

blocks.title: Secrets
blocks.text: No `.env` file is versioned; only `api/.env.example` and `web/.env.example`, with placeholders. The `api/.env` file exists only on the local machine and is in `.gitignore`.

blocks.title: To be confirmed

sections.title: Troubleshooting
sections.summary: Common problems and how to fix them.

rows: The API exits on start with "Variáveis de ambiente inválidas"
Check the `.env`. The error lists the invalid fields.
The front end shows "Não foi possível conectar ao servidor"
Start the API (`npm run dev` in `api/`) and check the URL. Restart Vite after changing the `.env`.
Front end on another port or `WEB_URL` differs from the origin
Use port 5173 or adjust `WEB_URL`, with no trailing slash.
Already configured in `buildApp.ts`; check that the local code was not changed.
Rate limit per IP and per minute
Point to a separate database, such as a Neon branch.
Serverless entry point or missing variables
Check `DATABASE_URL`, `JWT_SECRET` and `WEB_URL`. Read the function logs; the handler logs "Falha ao iniciar a API".
The Pix option disappears for customers
Enter the key under **Pix and contact** (with `MODO_DEMO=false`).
Set a secret with 16+ characters on Vercel.

sections.title: Architecture decisions
sections.summary: Relevant choices, with context and consequences, inferred from the code.

blocks.title: To be confirmed
blocks.text: These decisions were deduced from code comments and the git history. Review them with whoever made each decision.
1. Price computed only on the server

items: **Context:** the customer could tamper with values in the browser.
**Decision:** the API ignores any value sent and computes everything from the tiers and the configuration.
**Alternatives:** trust the total sent by the front end.
**Consequences:** the front end keeps a duplicated preview in `web/src/lib/preco.ts`, which must follow the API rules.

blocks.text: 2. API as a serverless function on Vercel

items: **Context:** simple, cheap deployment for a portfolio project.
**Decision:** `src/index.ts` exports a handler and reuses the Fastify instance; `server.ts` is kept for local use.
**Alternatives:** a traditional server (Fly.io, Railway, Render).
**Consequences:** the rate limit is per instance and approximate; the notification must be awaited before responding, because the function ends together with the response.

blocks.text: 3. Logo as base64 inside JSON, stored in the database

items: **Context:** avoid an upload plugin and external storage.
**Decision:** `PUT /marca/logo` receives base64 and stores `Bytes` in the `Configuracao` table.
**Alternatives:** `multipart/form-data` with object storage.
**Consequences:** works in serverless; size is limited to 300 KB.
**Context:** a single shop with few parameters.
**Decision:** the `Configuracao` table always has the row `id = 1`.
**Alternatives:** a key-value table or one table per topic.
**Consequences:** simple and typed; it does not support multiple shops without changing the model.

blocks.text: 5. Demo mode locked by an environment variable

items: **Context:** the dashboard is public and any visitor could enter real data.
**Decision:** `MODO_DEMO=true` fixes name, Pix, holder, bank and WhatsApp, and a cron deletes orders every day.
**Alternatives:** an invite-only dashboard.
**Consequences:** the app works for real with `MODO_DEMO=false`.

sections.summary: Domain terms used in the code and in the interface.

rows: An order with only a quantity, without choosing flavors. The shop decides.
A fixed amount for a quantity from 10 to 100 units.
An 8-character identifier the customer uses to track the order.
The customer collects the order at the shop address.
Date and time chosen by the customer. Without it, the order is "whenever it is ready".
Hours before the scheduled time by which the Pix must be paid.
The banknote value the customer hands over when paying in cash.
A switch that turns delivery off for the current day only.
A public setup where branding and Pix data are fixed and fictional.
A push notification service used to alert new orders.
